thread:
maria: Noticing recurring tail-latency sawtooth on prod-rt serving cluster, started ~03:15 UTC. Every ~6m there's a ~150-300ms tail jump for 99.9% on generation routes.
aj: What changed around that time? any deploys/rollouts?
maria: No deploys in the window. Topology steady. Rolling metrics attached: per-route p99 sawtooth. perf-bot: Alerting: p99 > 200ms on /v1/generate for customer-tier=hosted, spike period 6m, duration ~45s.
sanjay: Can you paste the scheduler metrics? admission queue length / microbatch sizes?
maria: quick dump:
```
admission.window_ms=50
microbatch.target=8
current_batch_sizes: avg=6.2 p90=8 p99=16
queue_depth spikes align with tail spike
kvcache.hits ~ stable
```
aj: Hmm p99=16 microbatches is weird. could be worker-level batching backlog
kevin: Also saw kernel selection churn in logs at same timestamps: dynamic-kernel-selector switched between fp16/quant kernels repeatedly.
eva: I ran a short repro on canary with load replay; toggling dynamic-kernel-selector off removes the sawtooth but increases steady p50 by ~30ms.
sanjay: So tradeoff: selector saves avg latency but causes periodic tail thrash. Why periodic? any background job? perf-bot: Scheduled job detected: nightly-kv-compact runs every 6 minutes in node pool 3 starting at 03:12 UTC (compactor v2). This correlates.
maria: compaction could evict/rehash KV pages causing cache misses and kernel fallback due to different memory alignment? strange.
aj: Can we confirm kvcache eviction counts around spike?
maria: evictions spike +2k during event (attached histogram). Also see a burst of allocation failures on GPU leading to kernel fallback to slower path.
kevin: Allocation failures -> kernel fallback -> higher compute per token -> batch queues grow -> microbatch sizes spike -> tail latency rises. Matches.
eva: Repro steps I used:
```
# local replay
GATEWAY=canary ./scripts/loadgen --profile=prod --duration=10m --rate=120
# toggle selector
kubectl set env deploy/worker DYNAMIC_KERNEL_SELECTOR=false -n runtime
```
result: sawtooth disappears.
sanjay: Temporary mitigation: increase admission.window_ms to 80 and cap microbatch max to 12. That should limit backlog while we fix compactor/eviction.
maria: Will open a hotfix PR to bump window and cap. Also propose draining compactor from that node pool.
kevin: Long-term: add kernel-selection hysteresis (don't switch kernels within 2m of prior switch) and add pre-check for alloc headroom before selecting high-throughput kernel.
eva: I'll capture pprof traces during next spike and upload. Also saved nvprof traces showing switching kernels' warmup costs.
perf-bot: Perf snapshot: p50 +28ms, p95 +40ms, p99 +210ms during spike. CPU: +12% system, GPU memory transient +600MB.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1472 link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1472
aj: Action items:
- maria: PR to bump admission.window_ms & max microbatch (hotfix) (owner: maria)
- kevin: prototype hysteresis / pre-check on selector (owner: kevin)
- eva: pprof + nvprof artifacts upload (owner: eva)
- sanjay: schedule compactor rate-limiting or node-drain (owner: sanjay)
- perf-bot: monitor p99 over next 6h and post updates
maria: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (reverts dynamic behavior for compactor-exposed nodes)
kevin: We'll canary the PR to pool-2 first.
eva: Uploaded traces: gs://redwood-perf/trace-1805432.tar.gz
sanjay: Noted — let's meet in 30 to triage results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks — keeping channel updated.
